issues: Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: Normalize user idea for a material study focusing on a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, preserving the original manufactured object's shape and silhouette with minimal transformation.

must_have: clear, readable contour evidence of a single manufactured object
exact form lock of the engineered object
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.framing: tight on the single manufactured object, preserving its full silhouette
composition.camera: neutral, eye-level perspective to clearly present the object
composition.background: minimalist, neutral, non-distracting background to highlight the subject and material

constraints: ensure full material readability across the object's surface
avoid harsh shadows or blown-out highlights that obscure material detail
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: abstract composition issues leading to subject loss
drift towards texture-only or atmosphere-first outcomes
loss of manufactured object readability due to material focus
unwanted material reads (e.g., plaster, glossy plastic)
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: lock the object read to a single, clearly defined manufactured object
prevent abstract drift or loss of form
strictly adhere to original shape, minimal transformation, and silhouette preservation
maintain material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read
suppress any visual cues suggesting plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: immediate and clear readability of a single manufactured object
clean matte B4C technical ceramic material read is dominant and accurate
dry, dense, engineered manufactured-object readability is preserved
original shape and silhouette of the object are clearly maintained
material-only scope is successfully achieved without losing the object's identity
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Focus on rendering a single, clearly defined engineered ceramic component with a clean matte B4C technical ceramic finish, strictly preserving its original shape and silhouette, while suppressing any abstract or unwanted material reads.
